events.title: Volunteer Day: Clara's Garden
events.location: Clara's Garden
events.description: GreenThumb community gardens are developed, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces.Clara's Garden is a quiet green oasis in East New York that is seeking volunteers to help build new garden beds and plant natives! Join us for a hands-on volunteer day! No prior experience necessary - beginners are welcome! Come learn about the neighborhood's community gardens. GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.This is a great opportunity to support a dynamic community space while learning about urban agriculture. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here! Register for Day 2 - Here! Location: 579 Glenmore Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11207For information about group volunteering, please contact Volunteer Program Coordinator, Olivia Navarro at Olivia.Navarro@parks.nyc.govThis event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: Forest Fitness
events.location: Margaret Corbin Circle (in Fort Tryon Park)
events.description: Join us for a free, year-round “Fitness at the Fort” exercise program on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays!This fitness class incorporates climbing multiple staircases, stretches and strengthening exercises, notable tree identification, and forest bathing. Led by instructor, Nancy Bruning, BA, MPH, PAPHS.Classes are structured so that all levels of fitness will be accommodated; however, all classes involve relatively brisk walking and some stairs because of the layout of the park itself. Classes vary according to the season, path conditions, and the weather, but always meet at the Heather Garden entrance.Tuesday and Thursday classes end at various points near the starting point, including the volleyball courts. Saturday class ends at the Anne Loftus Playground, using the various pieces of equipment, and offers optional after-class group walk to the Greenmarket on Isham Street. All classes end with closing with stretches.(Note: Fitness Walking does not meet if it is raining or if the actual temperature or wind chill is below 20 degrees F.)

events.title: Garden Conflict Transformation Circle— A 2-Month Journey for Community Gardeners | Session #2
events.location: Virtual/Online Workshop
events.description: Even the most harmonious garden groups experience conflict—it's as natural as weeds sprouting between the tomatoes. But what if those challenging moments could become opportunities for deeper connection and stronger communities? Join mediators Skye Roper-Moses and Michelle Jackson for an intimate, two-month learning cohort designed specifically for community gardeners who are ready to transform the way they navigate conflict.Session 1: Conflict Transformation CircleShare real-life challenges in a confidential, supportive space with fellow gardeners. Together, you’ll co-create solutions and learn practical skills you can take directly back to your garden.Session 2: Conflict Transformation Experiential LabDeepen your practice through hands-on exercises. Learn how to address tensions before they take root and gain confidence facilitating difficult conversations.Whether you’re facing personality clashes over plot boundaries or navigating group dynamics, this cohort will give you the tools to turn conflict into fertile ground for growth. Come ready to dig deep—transform challenges into connections. Register Here NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park
events.location: St. Mary's Annual 5K Start
events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

events.location: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
events.description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Called the “Gateway to the Bronx River,” 205-acre Soundview Park is located where the Bronx River opens into the East River. This urban green space is filled with grassy baseball and soccer fields, a cricket pitch, basketball courts, a running track, walking/biking paths, picnic fields, and more! With its extensive views of the water, Soundview Park celebrates the beauty of both the Bronx and East Rivers. The back part of our Open Run course has beautiful views of the Bronx River waterfront for participants to enjoy!

events.title: Planning an Event in Your Garden
events.location: Virtual/Online Workshop
events.description: Participants will learn:• How to identify the best type of event for their garden and community• How to create a realistic event plan from start to finish• Event planning basics, including timelines, logistics, and volunteer coordination• Ways to make events accessible and welcoming• Outreach and digital marketing strategies to increase participation• The different types of support available through GreenThumb• GreenThumb staff support and available resources, including for eligible SEED gardens• How to take advantage of citywide opportunities such as GreenThumb's Earth Month and Garden Day celebrationsParticipants will receive planning tools, templates, and resources to help turn their ideas into successful garden programs.Recommended for: New and experienced GreenThumb gardeners, garden leaders, and volunteers interested in hosting community events and educational programs. events.description: Join Fantasy Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a volunteer day cleaning up the garden, rebuilding raised beds (no power tools needed), and planting native flowers! Note some tasks will involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here!Fantasy Garden has been a public green space in the Brownsville for nearly three decades, providing the community with access to free programming, volunteer opportunities, and a connection to nature. events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Widely known for its history with the Crocheron Family and summer house, Crocheron Park is home to running paths, baseball fields, and a 4-court tennis center.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: NYRR Open Run: Highland Park
events.location: Elton Street and Jamaica Avenue (in Highland Park)
events.description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Located in the Cypress Hills section of Brooklyn, Highland Park is close to East New York and Bushwick in Brooklyn and the Woodhaven, Ridgewood, and Glendale neighborhoods in Queens. events.title: NYRR Open Run: Shore Road Park
events.location: Lawn Near 79th Street Entrance (in Shore Park and Parkway)
events.description: NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Shore Road Park, located in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, is one of our longer Open Run courses. events.title: NYRR Open Run: Soundview Park
events.location: Entrance - Lafayette Avenue and Morrison Avenue (in Soundview Park)
events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Called the “Gateway to the Bronx River,” 205-acre Soundview Park is located where the Bronx River opens into the East River. This urban green space is filled with grassy baseball and soccer fields, a cricket pitch, basketball courts, a running track, walking/biking paths, picnic fields, and more! With its extensive views of the water, Soundview Park celebrates the beauty of both the Bronx and East Rivers. The back part of our Open Run course has beautiful views of the Bronx River waterfront for participants to enjoy!
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.

events.title: Membership Meeting & Volunteer Workday
events.location: George Washington Carver Community Garden
events.description: Interested in being a garden volunteer? Fill out our Garden Interest Form!Join George Washington Carver Community Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for the last public workday of the 2026 growing season! This educational community garden is nestled in Williamsburg, Brooklyn and cared for by dedicated volunteers excited about urban gardening, composting, chicken care, and public programming. We’re looking for more dedicated folks ready to collaborate and get their hands in the dirt. Join us on this day to learn more!Volunteers will get involved in filling raised beds and planting cover crops! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note some tasks will involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here!For questions, please e-mail us at gwashingtoncarvergarden@gmail.com or gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov. Follow the garden on Instagram where we'll share our exciting progress! This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.
events.costNote: Organizer description states this program is free. Registration may be required.
